subject: Mid-ocean ridge
hook: MID-OCEAN RIDGE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The 'mid-ocean ridge' is a misnomer, as most of these ridges are not located in the middle of their respective ocean basins.
angle_support: The first discovered mid-ocean ridge was the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, which is a spreading center that bisects the North and South Atlantic basins; its location was the reason for the name "mid-ocean ridge".
Most oceanic spreading centers are not in the middle of their hosting ocean basins, but are traditionally called mid-ocean ridges regardless.
title: Why 'Mid-Ocean Ridge' is a Total Lie
description: The term 'mid-ocean ridge' implies a central location in every ocean basin, but this is a scientific misnomer. These massive tectonic features are defined by plate boundaries, not their proximity to the center of the ocean.
narration: MID-OCEAN RIDGE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a massive underwater mountain range perfectly centered between continents, dividing every ocean basin neatly in two. It was a logical guess when scientists first mapped the Atlantic. But in reality, this name is a geographic misnomer that ignores how the planet actually functions. While the Mid-Atlantic Ridge does sit centrally, most spreading centers are nowhere near the middle of their respective basins. The Pacific Ocean’s ridge system, for example, is pushed far to the east. These features are defined by tectonic plate boundaries, not by their distance from continental coastlines. Their global position is dictated by mantle processes, leaving them scattered across ocean floors wherever plates happen to pull apart. The name stuck because of one discovery, but the geology ignores our need for perfect symmetry.
